questions.title: Subarray Sums Equal to K
questions.description:
A telemetry parser counts how many contiguous sample windows sum exactly to k. Negative samples make sliding windows useless — prefix sums with a HashMap do it in one pass.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long countSubarrays(int[] a, int k)

Count the contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to exactly k.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and k.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the number of subarrays.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
-100 <= a[i] <= 100
-10000 <= k <= 10000

questions.title: Isomorphic Label Pair
questions.description:
Two product labels are isomorphic when the letters of one can be replaced (one-to-one) to obtain the other — egg and add qualify, foo and bar do not.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int isIsomorphic(String s, String t)

Return 1 if s and t are isomorphic (same length; each character of s maps to exactly one character of t and vice versa), else 0. Track both directions in HashMaps.

Input Format:
Line 1: string s.
Line 2: string t.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
s.length == t.length, 1 <= length <= 1000
lowercase letters

questions.title: Frequency of a Target
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int countTarget(int[] a, int target)

Count how many times target occurs in a. Build a frequency HashMap over the array and read the entry — that is the pattern being practised.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and target.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the frequency of target.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
-100 <= a[i] <= 100
-100 <= target <= 100

questions.title: First Duplicate Value
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int firstDuplicate(int[] a)

Scan a left to right and return the first value that has already been seen earlier in the scan; if every value is unique return -1. A HashSet of seen values makes this a one-pass job.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the first duplicate value or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
1 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Count of Distinct Values
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int distinctCount(int[] a)

Return the number of distinct values in a. Collect them into a HashSet and report its size.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the number of distinct values.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
1 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Key Value Lookups
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] lookupValues(int[] keys, int[] values, int[] queries)

Build a HashMap mapping keys[i] to values[i] (keys are distinct), then answer every query with its value, or -1 when the key is absent. Return the answers in query order.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and q.
Line 2: n distinct keys.
Line 3: n values (values[i] belongs to keys[i]).
Line 4: q query keys.

Output Format:
One line with q answers, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, q <= 1000
1 <= keys[i], queries[i] <= 100000 (keys distinct)
1 <= values[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Longest Consecutive Run
questions.description:
A uptime monitor compresses its log into the longest run of consecutive integer days present in the data — order in the log does not matter.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int longestConsecutive(int[] a)

Return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive integers that all occur in a. A HashSet gives O(n) without sorting.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the longest consecutive run length.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
-100000 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Hash Bucket Occupancy
questions.description:
A toy hash table with m buckets hashes every value with h(v) = v mod m. Collisions simply pile up in the same bucket. Count how many values land in each bucket.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] bucketCounts(int[] a, int m)

Return the occupancy of buckets 0, 1, ..., m-1 (all values are non-negative). This is the count array of a modulo hash.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and m.
Line 2: n space-separated non-negative integers.

Output Format:
One line with m bucket counts, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
1 <= m <= 100
0 <= a[i] <= 100000

questions.title: Most Frequent Character
questions.description:
The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static char mostFrequent(String s)

Return the character that occurs most often in s (lowercase letters). If several characters tie for the highest frequency, return the lexicographically smallest of them — this keeps the answer deterministic.

Input Format:
One line: the string s.

Output Format:
One line: the most frequent character.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 10000
s contains lowercase letters

questions.title: Duplicate Username Alert
questions.description:
A sign-up service rejects registration when a username already exists in the session registry. You flag sessions where somebody tried a name twice.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int seenBefore(String[] users)

Return 1 if any username appears at least twice in the list, else 0.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated usernames.

Output Format:
One line: 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= users[i].length <= 20
usernames contain lowercase letters and digits
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, usernames: lowercase letters and digits

questions.title: Candidate Vote Tally
questions.description:
A club election stores every ballot in a log. The returning officer asks for the number of votes one candidate received.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int tallyVotes(String[] votes, String target)

Count how many entries of votes equal target. Build the full frequency map first — that is the drill.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n (ballots) — then the target name on the same line.
Line 2: n space-separated candidate names.

Output Format:
One line: the vote count for target.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000
1 <= names.length <= 20, lowercase letters
questions.sampleinput1:
5 mia
mia jo mia sam jo

questions.title: Students in Both Sections
questions.description:
A school office compares the roll calls of two class sections and wants to know how many students attend both.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int commonNames(String[] a, String[] b)

Count the number of distinct names that appear in both lists.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and m.
Line 2: n space-separated names of section A.
Line 3: m space-separated names of section B.

Output Format:
One line: the number of common distinct names.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 1000
names: lowercase letters

3 3
ana bob cid
bob cid dan

a b c d
c d

tam tom tim tim

questions.title: Coupon Code Validation
questions.description:
A shop tracks redeemed coupon codes. At checkout it verifies each presented code against the redeemed set and counts the valid ones.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int validRedemptions(String[] redeemed, String[] queries)

Count how many query codes exist in the redeemed set.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and q.
Line 2: n space-separated redeemed codes.
Line 3: q space-separated query codes.

Output Format:
One line: how many queries are in the redeemed set.

Constraints:
1 <= n, q <= 1000
codes: lowercase letters and digits
questions.sampleinput1:
3 4
save10 mega bonus
save10 fail mega none
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n, q <= 1000, lowercase letters and digits

questions.title: Count Pairs With Given Sum
questions.description:
A logistics planner counts delivery pairs whose route costs add up to a target. Pairs are unordered index pairs (i < j).

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static long countPairs(int[] a, int target)

Count the pairs (i, j) with i < j and a[i] + a[j] == target. Use one HashMap pass: for each value add the frequency of its complement seen so far.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and target.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: the number of pairs.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
-100 <= a[i] <= 100
-200 <= target <= 200

questions.title: Ordered Keys of a Registry
questions.description:
A range registry must always answer with its keys in sorted order, so it is backed by a TreeMap (sorted map). Replay the operations and report the surviving keys.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static ArrayList<Integer> finalKeys(String[] ops, int[] vals)

ops[i] is "p" (put key vals[i]) or "e" (erase key vals[i]; erasing an absent key does nothing). Return the keys still present, in ascending order. Use a TreeMap — HashMap gives no ordering. The harness prints EMPTY when the list is empty.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer m (number of operations).
Line 2: m operation letters (p or e).
Line 3: m keys (vals[i] for op i).

Output Format:
One line with the remaining keys ascending, or EMPTY.

Constraints:
1 <= m <= 1000
1 <= keys <= 100000
questions.input2:
6
p p p e e e
1 2 3 1 2 3

questions.title: Sort by Frequency
questions.description:
A playlist analyser orders song ids by play count: most played first, ties broken by smaller id first. Every id appears once in the output.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] frequencySort(int[] a)

Return the distinct values of a ordered by frequency (descending), ties by value (ascending).

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the ordered distinct values, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
1 <= a[i] <= 100

questions.title: Two-Sum Positions
questions.description:
A payment reconciler locates the two transactions that cancel a target amount and needs their positions in the ledger.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] twoSumIndices(int[] a, int target)

Return the indices i < j with a[i] + a[j] == target, choosing the pair with the smallest second index j (and the earliest possible i for that j). Return [-1, -1] when no pair exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and target.
Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line: "i j" or "-1 -1".

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
-1000 <= a[i] <= 1000
-2000 <= target <= 2000

questions.title: Union and Intersection Sizes
questions.description:
A permissions auditor compares two access-id lists and reports how many ids exist in at least one list and how many exist in both.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int[] unionIntersection(int[] a, int[] b)

Return [unionSize, intersectionSize] where both sizes count distinct ids. Build HashSets and count with loops (no retainAll / addAll shortcuts).

Input Format:
Line 1: integers n and m.
Line 2: n space-separated ids.
Line 3: m space-separated ids.

Output Format:
One line: union size and intersection size, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 10000
1 <= ids <= 100000

questions.title: Longest Run Without Repeats
questions.description:
A telemetry key viewer scans a stream of characters and reports the longest stretch without any repeated character — a classic sliding window over a set.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int longestUnique(String s)

Return the length of the longest substring of s in which every character occurs at most once.

Input Format:
One line: the string s.

Output Format:
One line: the longest unique substring length.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 100
s contains lowercase letters

questions.title: Longest Substring With K Distinct
questions.description:
A cache profiler measures the longest stretch of a request log containing at most k distinct endpoints.

The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int longestKDistinct(String s, int k)

Return the length of the longest substring of s with at most k distinct characters (k >= 1).

Input Format:
Line 1: the string s.
Line 2: integer k.

Output Format:
One line: the length.

Constraints:
1 <= s.length <= 100
1 <= k <= 26
s contains lowercase letters
